_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MOSTLY ROCK. Roughly three quarters of this tile is one continuous mountain wall -- pale silk built up with long wandering 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes, its ridges and folds picked out with 点苔 moss dabs. All the real foliage is crammed into the bottom-left quadrant and the bottom edge, plus one row of trees along the ridge at the top right. THE HARD CALL IN THIS TILE, and the reason it is worth reading this note before trusting any mask: there are FOUR different things here that all look like distant trees at thumbnail size, and only ONE of them is. (1) REAL, at x 0.635-0.81, y 0.065-0.175: a fringe of pines along the top-right ridge. Zoomed 6x these resolve into flat layered 松 crowns sitting on pale vertical trunks -- the wood is genuinely visible in the gaps between canopy layers. Catalogued as a tree, but as a SEARCH REGION and with a warning: no single crown in that row is wider than about 0.03 of the tile, so the row can only be moved as one soft mass, never per-tree. (2) NOT REAL, at x 0.82-1.0, y 0.0-0.16: the row continues right but degenerates into single tapered vertical brush strokes -- one stroke IS one whole far tree, about 0.012 of the tile wide, with no separable leaf mass at all. Left inside the rock ridge object on purpose. (3) NOT REAL, the whole right cliff x 0.60-1.0, y 0.10-0.62: at 5x this is 点苔 dotting strung along the cliff's contour folds, plus fans of hemp-fibre strokes. It is the single largest false-positive surface in these three tiles and it is the family of mark that made the rock move in the earlier pass. (4) NOT REAL, x 0.70-1.0, y 0.60-0.85: a bare slope of fine parallel downhill strokes with a handful of smeared dabs -- reads as hanging needles, contains no leaf glyph and no wood. The genuine foliage, all of it in the bottom band: a great blue-green tree at centre-right whose ochre trunk and right-sweeping limb are unmistakable (and whose bare 蟹爪 claw-branches poke up above the canopy at x 0.475-0.55, y 0.60-0.665 -- wood, not leaves); a tight autumn grove at bottom-left in three colours, yellow-ochre, red-orange and tan, all drawn as 夾葉 double-outline leaves; a blue-green leaf mass along the bottom edge; a dark pine clump at x 0.51-0.63; an orange autumn canopy at bottom-centre-right; and a blue-green mass clipped by the right edge that continues into t011. The dark trees at the extreme left edge, x 0.0-0.095, are the same trees catalogued in t009 as cliff-pines-right and ridge-grove-bottom-right -- these tiles overlap by 12% and those two entries are the SAME objects seen twice. One bare branching tree with no leaves stands at x 0.19-0.26, y 0.795-0.865 and is recorded as trunk so a leaf animator skips it.

objects.name: great rock wall, left third
objects.note: pale silk with long vertical hemp-fibre contours describing a fold that runs the full height. Almost no dotting here, which is why it is the least deceptive part of the wall. Clipped by the top and left edges

objects.name: great rock wall, centre
objects.note: the main body of the mountain; layered ledges in wandering contour with light dotting along each ledge lip. Entirely rigid

objects.name: dotted cliff shoulder, right
objects.note: DECOY (3) FROM THE TILE NOTE, and the biggest false-positive surface in this set. Dense 点苔 moss dabs run along every contour fold, and at thumbnail size the strings of dabs read as ranks of distant pines. Verified at 5x: dabs and hemp-fibre only, no stem, no branch, no leaf glyph anywhere. NEVER animate

objects.name: ridge crest with single-stroke far trees, upper right
objects.note: DECOY (2). Deliberately labelled rock even though it contains trees: the far trees here are single tapered vertical brush strokes, roughly 0.012 of the tile wide, with no leaf mass separable from the stroke that draws the whole tree. Far under the size floor and unanimatable. Clipped by the top and right edges

objects.name: row of pines along the top-right ridge
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, AND THE ONLY REAL FOLIAGE IN THE TOP HALF OF THIS TILE. At 6x each form resolves into a flat layered pine crown with a pale vertical trunk showing in the gap beneath it -- genuine wood, checked specifically because the surrounding cliff is full of look-alike dotting. Caveat that matters: individual crowns are only about 0.024-0.033 of the tile across, under the 0.06 floor, so this row must be treated as ONE soft mass. Animating per-tree would read as jitter, and the ridge rock inside the box would come with it

objects.name: dark cliff trees clipped by the left edge
objects.note: the right-hand end of the pine row catalogued in summit-t009.json as cliff-pines-right -- SAME OBJECT, seen again in the 12% overlap between these tiles. Dark flat canopies over pale trunks. Do not double-count it when merging tiles

objects.name: pine grove clipped by the bottom left corner
objects.note: the same grove catalogued in summit-t009.json as ridge-grove-bottom-right -- SAME OBJECT in the tile overlap. Unambiguous dark vertical trunks with spreading crowns

objects.name: bare branching tree on the slope, centre left
objects.note: a small 蟹爪 crab-claw tree drawn as trunk plus forking bare branches with no leaf marks on them at all. Real wood, zero foliage -- recorded so a leaf pass skips it rather than mistaking the branch tangle for a sparse canopy

objects.name: yellow-ochre autumn canopy, bottom left
objects.note: dense tangled leaf strokes under a bright yellow-ochre wash. Sits directly above and behind the red-orange canopy; the two are different trees in the same grove and their masses interlock, so a tight boundary between them does not exist

objects.name: red-orange autumn canopy, bottom left
objects.note: small rectangular scale-like leaf marks under a strong red-orange wash -- the most saturated passage in the tile. Clipped by the bottom edge, continues below this band

objects.name: tan autumn canopy, right of the yellow one
objects.note: peach-tan wash over the same tangled leaf stroke as its neighbours; the third crown of the bottom-left grove. Its right edge meets the blue-green tree's lower leaves around x 0.51

objects.name: blue-green leaf mass along the bottom edge, centre
objects.note: rounded blue-green 夾葉 clusters filling the bottom edge below the autumn grove. Clipped by the bottom edge; the wood belonging to it is out of frame below, so trust the leaf glyphs rather than looking for a trunk here

objects.name: crown of the great blue-green tree, centre right
objects.note: broad canopy of small blue-green leaf strokes spreading right from the trunk. The best-evidenced tree in the tile: its ochre trunk and its right-sweeping limb are both plainly visible inside this box and are wood, not leaves

objects.name: lower leaf curtain of the blue-green tree
objects.note: the canopy hanging below the main limb; left edge reaches x 0.42 where it overlaps the tan autumn crown. Bottom edge at y 0.795 is where leaves stop and bare slope begins

objects.name: ochre trunk of the blue-green tree
objects.note: a clear pale-ochre vertical stem running from the fork down through the canopy to the slope. Narrow, but this is the wood that makes the two leaf boxes above a tree. RIGID

objects.name: limb sweeping right out of the blue-green tree
objects.note: a long ochre bough running out to the right through the canopy, visible in every gap between leaf clusters. A hinge should pivot the leaves about this line

objects.name: bare claw branches above the blue-green canopy
objects.note: dark 蟹爪 crab-claw twigs rising out of the top of the tree above the leaf line, against empty silk. They look like a thin dark spray and will be swept up by any dark-ink mask built for the canopy -- exclude them, they are wood

objects.name: dark pine clump below the blue-green tree
objects.note: a dense dark-ink clump on the slope with trunk strokes legible at its base. SEARCH REGION -- it stands on open rock and roughly a third of this box is stone

objects.name: orange autumn canopy, bottom centre right
objects.note: salmon-orange wash over tangled leaf strokes, clipped by the bottom edge. Isolated on bare rock, so its silhouette is clean on the left, top and right -- a good sway subject despite being cut off below

objects.name: blue-green leaf mass clipped by the right edge
objects.note: rounded blue-green 夾葉 clusters with dark outlines running down the right edge. The wood belonging to them is out of frame to the right; it is visible in t011, where the same mass is catalogued again

objects.name: open rock slope, lower left
objects.note: pale contoured ledges scattered with small dark texture strokes. The little wispy marks through here are 苔點 on stone, not distant leaves

objects.name: bare hemp-fibre slope, lower right
objects.note: DECOY (4). Fine parallel strokes running downhill across a wide empty slope, with a few smeared dabs. Checked at 5x: not one leaf glyph, no wood. It sits directly above the real orange canopy at bottom-centre-right, so this is the pair a mask is most likely to merge by mistake

objects.name: rock ground between the pine clump and the orange canopy
objects.note: the ground the bottom-band trees stand on; pale contoured stone clipped by the bottom edge
